assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology through to incretin-based drugs is a rare unbroken line from basic hormone biology (proglucagon processing, the incretin effect, insulinotropic action of GLP-1) to therapies that have changed the treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with large cardiovascular and renal outcome benefits. Originality, clarity and lasting impact are all high.
assessment.attribution: Holst established GLP-1 physiology in humans, Drucker defined its biology and therapeutic logic including GLP-2 and DPP-4 pathways, and Knudsen led the design of long-acting acylated analogues (liraglutide, semaglutide). Mojsov's contribution to identifying the active peptide form is real but its relative weight is disputed, and others outside the supplied list (e.g. Habener) are likely involved; the cap of three forces a hard choice.
assessment.maturity: Clinical efficacy has been confirmed independently and at massive scale over many years; the mechanisms are well understood. Recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Credit allocation among Holst, Drucker, Mojsov and Knudsen is contested and I am relying on recalled rather than verified history.
Whether a basic-science-plus-drug-design configuration is preferred to a purely physiological one is unresolved.
Long-term safety and mechanism details of central effects are still evolving.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells as living drugs opened a new therapeutic modality, with durable remissions in refractory B-cell leukemias and lymphomas and now myeloma, and recent signals in autoimmunity. Conceptually original and clinically transformative.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain pioneered CD28 co-stimulated CARs and the preclinical framework, June led the first successful 4-1BB CD19 CAR-T clinical translation, and Rosenberg pioneered adoptive cell therapy and early CAR trials. Eshhar, Kuwana and others whose early work underlies CARs are not in the supplied credit, so any configuration is incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and years of follow-up confirm efficacy in hematologic malignancies. Solid tumours, toxicity and manufacturing limits remain, but the core discovery is mature.
uncertainties: Foundational CAR concept credit outside the supplied names may be needed for fairness.
Choosing among three overlapping clinical and preclinical contributions is subjective.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response revealed a new intracellular signalling pathway from ER to nucleus, with IRE1, XBP1 splicing, ATF6 and PERK, linking proteostasis to disease in diabetes, neurodegeneration and cancer. Highly original, clear and fundamental.
assessment.attribution: Mori identified the transcriptional response and ER stress element signalling, Walter identified IRE1 and the unconventional splicing mechanism and later ISRIB. The pairing is natural and coherent; Kozutsumi and others contributed early.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism has been confirmed repeatedly over three decades and is textbook; translational payoff is still emerging, which does not reduce basic-science standing.
uncertainties: Whether a basic-mechanism prize is favoured over a clinically impactful one this year.
Early contributors beyond the two names might be argued.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: HPV virus-like-particle vaccines prevent persistent infection and cervical and other HPV-related cancers; real-world data show dramatic reductions in precancer and now invasive cancer. This is a clear major benefit to mankind based on a clever and original capsid self-assembly insight.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller developed L1 VLPs at NCI; Frazer and Zhou developed VLP expression and the Australian line of work. Zhou Jian is deceased and not on the list; Harald zur Hausen was already recognised for the causal virus link. Three names are plausible but the Frazer versus other-group credit is contested.
assessment.maturity: Population-level effectiveness confirmed independently across countries and over about 15 years; clearly mature.
uncertainties: Legal and priority disputes among VLP developers complicate fair attribution.
Whether the committee views this as sufficiently distinct from the earlier HPV prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense oligonucleotide correction of SMN2 splicing (nusinersen) turned a fatal childhood disease into a treatable one and established splicing modulation as a drug mechanism. A strong combination of RNA-processing mechanism and clinical transformation, and a template for other antisense drugs.
assessment.attribution: Krainer defined the splicing regulatory elements and ISS-N1 target concept, Bennett led the antisense chemistry and development. The pairing is clean; Ionis and Biogen teams and other academic discoverers (e.g. Singh, Hua) are not credited.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with long-term follow-up data showing durable benefit; relatively recent but well confirmed.
uncertainties: Whether the novelty is judged to lie in the splicing mechanism or in the chemistry platform.
Comparatively recent timing may favour waiting.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Adult-stem-cell-derived organoids from Lgr5 stem cells created a widely used platform for tissue biology, disease modelling, drug testing and personalised medicine. Original, practical and enabling across many fields.
assessment.attribution: Clevers identified Lgr5 stem cells and led development of long-term intestinal organoids; Sato was first author of the pivotal 2009 work. Whether to credit both or Clevers alone is a judgement call; Yamanaka-type stem cell recognition and others (Sasai, Lancaster) are separate lines.
assessment.maturity: Method is thoroughly reproduced and in global use; clinical translation is still developing.
uncertainties: Overlap with other organoid and stem cell work is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Establishing that thymus-derived T cells and bursa-derived (marrow in mammals) B cells are distinct lineages is the foundation of modern adaptive immunology and underpins immunodeficiency diagnosis and immunotherapy.
assessment.attribution: Miller defined thymus function and T cells; Cooper (with Good and Peterson) defined the B-cell lineage. Robert Good is deceased and excluded; the pair is coherent and fair for the two lineages.
assessment.maturity: Very mature and universally confirmed; the age of the discovery raises timing concerns but also a risk of missing living laureates.
uncertainties: Contributions of deceased scientists complicate fairness.
Age of the discovery against later immunology prizes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib and BCR-ABL inhibition converted CML from fatal to chronic disease and proved the principle of molecularly targeted cancer therapy. Clear, transformative and original in clinical proof of concept.
assessment.attribution: Lydon led compound discovery, Druker established clinical proof and trials, Sawyers defined resistance mechanisms and next-generation inhibitors. Rowley, Nowell, Witte and Gleevec chemists are outside this credit set, so the BCR-ABL story is partly previously honoured or missing.
assessment.maturity: Outcomes are confirmed over two decades; maturity is high and recognition arguably late.
uncertainties: Whether the discovery is seen as incremental after earlier cancer-genetic work.
Sawyers versus others in the three-person configuration is debatable.
